attributes.name: revenue_stream_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.revenue_stream. Business justification: R&F reports validate revenue stream performance against sold audience guarantees. Finance uses these reports to reconcile revenue recognition with actual audience delivery for revenue assurance and au

attributes.name: title_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.title. Business justification: Reach and frequency reports are generated per program/title as standard post-buy advertiser deliverables. Linking to content.title enables program-level R&F analysis, content performance benchmarking

attributes.name: audience_share_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total viewing audience (persons using television) that was watching the specific network or program during the measurement period. Calculated as the program's audience divided by the total HUT/PUT audience. Used for competitive programming analysis and ad sales positioning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: average_frequency
attributes.description: The average number of times a unique viewer within the target demographic was exposed to the content or campaign during the measurement period. Calculated as total impressions divided by unduplicated reach. Core metric for evaluating campaign saturation and makegoods calculation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: cpm
attributes.description: The cost per one thousand audience impressions for the campaign or programming block, expressed in USD. Used by ad sales for post-campaign delivery validation, scatter market pricing justification, and makegood valuation. Confidential as it reflects negotiated commercial pricing.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Salesforce Media Cloud

attributes.name: cprp
attributes.description: The cost per one rating point delivered against the target demographic segment, expressed in USD. The primary pricing metric for linear TV advertising transactions. Used for upfront guarantee reconciliation, makegood valuation, and scatter market pricing. Confidential as it reflects negotiated commercial pricing.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this reach and frequency report record was first ingested into the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for data lineage tracking and pipeline monitoring.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Internal Data Standards; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary values in this report (CPM, CPRP). Defaults to USD for domestic US markets. Required for international market reports and multi-currency financial reconciliation under SOX compliance.

attributes.name: delivery_variance_pct
attributes.description: The percentage difference between the guaranteed audience delivery (GRP or TRP) and the actual delivered audience for the campaign flight. A negative value indicates under-delivery triggering makegood obligations; a positive value indicates over-delivery. Used for upfront guarantee reconciliation and scatter market adjustments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines; Wide Orbit

attributes.name: effective_reach_1plus
attributes.description: The count of unique persons exposed to the content or campaign at least one time (1+) during the measurement period. Equivalent to reach_persons; included as an explicit effective reach threshold field for consistency with N+ reporting framework used in post-campaign analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_reach_3plus
attributes.description: The count of unique persons exposed to the content or campaign at least three times (3+) during the measurement period. The industry-standard effective reach threshold used to assess whether sufficient frequency was achieved for advertising message recall. Critical for makegoods determination and campaign effectiveness evaluation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_reach_nplus
attributes.description: The count of unique persons exposed to the content or campaign at least N times (as defined by effective_reach_threshold) during the measurement period. Provides a configurable effective reach metric for custom campaign guarantee structures and advanced frequency analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_reach_threshold
attributes.description: The minimum number of exposures (N) used to define effective reach for this specific report. Configurable per campaign or client agreement (e.g., 3 for standard campaigns, 5 for high-frequency campaigns). Determines the N+ threshold applied in effective reach calculations beyond the standard 1+ and 3+ fields.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: grp
attributes.description: The sum of all rating points delivered by the campaign or programming block during the measurement period, representing total audience weight without deduplication. Calculated as reach percentage multiplied by average frequency. The primary currency for linear TV advertising transactions and upfront sales guarantees.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: hut_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of all television households in the market that had their television sets in use during the measurement period. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used as a contextual benchmark for evaluating audience share and competitive programming performance.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: is_makegood_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reach and frequency report has identified an audience delivery shortfall that requires a makegood (compensatory ad spot) to be issued to the advertiser. Triggers the makegood workflow in Wide Orbit and Salesforce Media Cloud when set to True.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing System; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Indicates whether the measurement period falls within a Nielsen sweeps period (an intensive ratings measurement period typically occurring in February, May, July, and November). Sweeps data carries elevated importance for programming decisions, ad rate setting, and affiliate compensation calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: measurement_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the measurement window for which reach and frequency metrics are computed. Defines the end boundary of the campaign flight, programming block, or sweeps period being analyzed.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: measurement_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the measurement window for which reach and frequency metrics are computed. Defines the start boundary of the campaign flight, programming block, or sweeps period being analyzed. Used in conjunction with measurement_period_end_date to bound the audience measurement interval.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: measurement_type
attributes.description: Classifies the type of measurement window for which this report was generated. 'campaign_flight' covers a defined ad campaign run; 'programming_block' covers a scheduled content block; 'daypart_window' covers a standard broadcast daypart; 'sweeps_period' covers an intensive Nielsen ratings measurement period; 'custom_window' covers an ad hoc analysis window.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: nielsen_report_code
attributes.description: The native report identifier assigned by the Nielsen Media Research Platform for this reach and frequency dataset. Used for source system traceability, data lineage, and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the Nielsen source system.

attributes.name: put_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of all persons in the target demographic who were watching television during the measurement period. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used alongside HUT to assess total available audience and calculate audience share for programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: reach_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the target demographic universe reached at least once during the measurement period, calculated as (reach_persons / universe_estimate) × 100. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 45.2500 = 45.25%). Used by ad sales for post-campaign delivery reporting and scatter market pricing justification.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: reach_persons
attributes.description: The unduplicated count of unique persons within the target demographic segment who were exposed to the content or campaign at least once during the measurement period. The primary reach metric sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used for post-campaign delivery validation and upfront guarantee reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_generated_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal real-world event timestamp when this reach and frequency report was generated and delivered by the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Represents the business event time, distinct from audit timestamps. Used to track Nielsen data delivery SLAs and post-campaign reporting timeliness.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this reach and frequency report, sourced from the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used by ad sales teams to reference specific post-campaign delivery reports in client communications, makegoods negotiations, and upfront guarantee reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the reach and frequency report. 'draft' indicates in-progress computation; 'preliminary' indicates initial Nielsen delivery pending validation; 'final' indicates validated and approved for client delivery; 'revised' indicates a corrected reissue; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer version; 'archived' indicates retired from active use.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_version
attributes.description: The version number of this reach and frequency report, incremented each time a revised or corrected report is issued by Nielsen or reprocessed in the lakehouse. Version 1 represents the initial delivery; subsequent versions represent corrections or revisions. Used to ensure ad sales teams are working with the most current data.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Media Broadcasting Internal Data Standards

attributes.name: total_impressions
attributes.description: The total number of audience exposures (duplicated) to the content or campaign during the measurement period. Equals reach_persons multiplied by average_frequency. Used as the gross delivery metric for CPM-based advertising transactions and campaign pacing analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Digital Advertising Standards

attributes.name: trp
attributes.description: The sum of rating points delivered specifically against the target demographic segment during the measurement period. Analogous to GRP but scoped to the defined target audience rather than the total population. Used for targeted advertising guarantee reconciliation and CPRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: universe_estimate
attributes.description: The total estimated population size (in persons or households) of the target demographic segment in the specified market, as defined by Nielsen. Serves as the denominator for reach percentage calculations and rating point computations. Expressed as an absolute count.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this reach and frequency report record was last modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Tracks revisions, status changes, and data corrections.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Internal Data Standards; SOX Compliance

products.name: market_coverage
products.description: Master record defining a Designated Market Area (DMA) or television market — the geographic unit used for local audience measurement. Captures DMA rank, DMA code, market name, TV household universe estimate, population universe, geographic boundaries, and applicable measurement methodology (PPM vs. diary). Aligns with Nielsen DMA definitions and FCC market designations for must-carry and retransmission consent compliance.

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the market coverage record representing a Designated Market Area (DMA) or television market geographic unit.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: broadcast_license_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.broadcast_license. Business justification: Market coverage definitions derive from broadcast license service contours and DMA assignments. License technical parameters (power, antenna height) determine market boundaries for audience measuremen

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.legal_entity. Business justification: Broadcast markets are served by specific licensed legal entities. FCC broadcast licenses and must-carry obligations are entity-specific, requiring direct link for regulatory filing and compliance repo

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Market coverage areas determine applicable regulatory obligations (must-carry, retransmission consent). DMA and market type drive specific FCC obligations; links market definitions to compliance requi

attributes.name: sales_territory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sales.sales_territory. Business justification: Sales territories are defined by geographic market boundaries (DMA codes). Territory planning, quota allocation, rep assignment, and market-based revenue forecasting all require knowing which market_c

attributes.name: blackout_rule_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether geographic broadcast blackout rules apply to this market for sports or syndication exclusivity purposes. True if blackout restrictions can be enforced in this DMA; False otherwise. Used by rights management (Rightsline) and CDN geo-restriction (Akamai) to enforce territorial exclusivity.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76.111; Rightsline Rights Management; Sports Blackout Rules

attributes.name: broadcast_standard
attributes.description: Digital broadcast transmission standard applicable to this market. 'ATSC' (Advanced Television Systems Committee) is the US standard; 'DVB' (Digital Video Broadcasting) is the European standard; 'ISDB' is the Japanese/Brazilian standard; 'DTMB' is the Chinese standard. Determines technical playout and transmission requirements.
attributes.references: ATSC Standards; DVB Project Standards; ISO/IEC 13818

attributes.name: cable_penetration_rate
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of television households in the DMA that subscribe to cable television (MVPD or vMVPD service). Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.6234 = 62.34%). Used for carriage fee negotiations, distribution planning, and ad sales reach projections.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates; FCC Annual Video Competition Report

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code identifying the country in which this market is located (e.g., 'USA', 'GBR', 'CAN'). Required for international rights management, windowing decisions, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.

attributes.name: daylight_saving_observed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DMA observes Daylight Saving Time (DST). True if DST is observed; False if not (e.g., markets in Arizona). Affects daypart scheduling, playout timing, and EPG accuracy in broadcast automation systems.

attributes.name: dma_code
attributes.description: Nielsen-assigned three-digit numeric code uniquely identifying the Designated Market Area (DMA). This is the externally-known business identifier used across ad sales, ratings reporting, and FCC filings. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC 47 CFR Part 76

attributes.name: dma_rank
attributes.description: Nielsen-assigned national rank of the DMA by television household universe size, where rank 1 is the largest market (New York). Used for market prioritization in ad sales, upfront negotiations, and carriage fee calculations. Updated annually by Nielsen.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The date from which this market coverage record became effective and the DMA definition was valid. Used for temporal versioning of DMA boundary and universe changes, ensuring historical ratings data is associated with the correct market definition.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The date on which this market coverage record ceased to be effective, typically due to a DMA boundary redefinition, market merger, or discontinuation. Null for currently active market definitions. Supports slowly changing dimension (SCD) history tracking.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: fcc_market_code
attributes.description: FCC-assigned market identifier used for must-carry and retransmission consent compliance filings. Maps the Nielsen DMA to the FCC's designated market definition for broadcast licensing, spectrum regulation, and MVPD carriage obligations. Required for regulatory reporting under FCC 47 CFR Part 76.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: geographic_boundary_wkt
attributes.description: Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the DMA's geographic boundary polygon. Used for spatial analysis, blackout rule enforcement, retransmission consent territory mapping, and OTT/streaming geo-restriction via CDN (Akamai). Conforms to OGC WKT standard.
attributes.references: OGC Well-Known Text Standard; FCC 47 CFR Part 76; Nielsen DMA Boundary Definitions

attributes.name: hispanic_tv_household_pct
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of television households in the DMA that are Hispanic/Latino, as measured by Nielsen. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.2341 = 23.41%). Used for Spanish-language content distribution decisions, targeted ad sales, and TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations for Hispanic demographic segments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Hispanic TV Audience Measurement; Nielsen Universe Estimates

attributes.name: hut_base_estimate
attributes.description: Nielsen baseline estimate of the percentage of television households in the DMA that are using television during an average primetime daypart. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.5823 = 58.23%). Used as a reference benchmark for HUT-based audience projections and ad sales planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen HUT Methodology

attributes.name: market_name
attributes.description: Official human-readable name of the Designated Market Area (DMA) or television market as defined by Nielsen (e.g., 'New York', 'Los Angeles', 'Chicago'). Used in audience reports, ad sales proposals, and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: market_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the market coverage record. 'active' indicates the DMA is currently measured and used in audience reporting; 'inactive' indicates it is no longer measured; 'pending' indicates a newly defined market awaiting first measurement; 'discontinued' indicates a market that has been merged or eliminated by Nielsen.

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: Classification of the market scope. 'local' indicates a single-city DMA; 'regional' indicates a multi-city or multi-state DMA; 'national' indicates a national aggregate market; 'international' indicates a non-US market territory. Used for ad sales segmentation, carriage fee tiers, and programming distribution decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: measurement_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which Nielsen provides audience measurement data for this market. 'continuous' indicates year-round metered measurement (PPM markets); 'sweeps_only' indicates measurement only during sweeps periods (diary markets); 'quarterly' or 'annual' for smaller markets with less frequent measurement cycles.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Measurement; Nielsen PPM and Diary Methodology

attributes.name: measurement_methodology
attributes.description: Nielsen measurement methodology applied to this market. 'PPM' (Portable People Meter) is the electronic passive measurement used in large markets; 'diary' is the paper-based recall method used in smaller markets; 'hybrid' indicates a combination of both. Determines the precision and frequency of ratings data available for this market.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen PPM Methodology; Nielsen Diary Methodology

attributes.name: median_household_income
attributes.description: Median annual household income (in USD) for the DMA, sourced from U.S. Census Bureau data as incorporated into Nielsen demographic profiles. Used for audience demographic segmentation, CPM (Cost Per Mille) pricing tiers, and advertiser targeting qualification.
attributes.references: U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey; Nielsen Demographic Profiles

attributes.name: must_carry_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether FCC must-carry rules apply to broadcast stations in this market, requiring cable operators (MVPDs) to carry local broadcast signals. True if must-carry obligations exist; False otherwise. Critical for retransmission consent negotiations and MVPD carriage compliance.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76 Subpart D; Cable Television Consumer Protection and Competition Act of 1992

attributes.name: nielsen_source_market_code
attributes.description: The native market identifier as assigned and used within the Nielsen Media Research Platform source system. Used for data lineage, reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the Nielsen source system, and audit of universe estimate ingestion.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Dalet Galaxy MAM Integration

attributes.name: nielsen_station_index
attributes.description: Total number of television stations measured by Nielsen within this DMA. Indicates the competitive landscape of the local market and is used in share calculations and ad sales competitive analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Measurement; Nielsen Station Index

attributes.name: ott_penetration_rate
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of television households in the DMA that access video content via OTT (Over-The-Top) streaming services. Expressed as a decimal. Used for digital distribution planning, SVOD/AVOD audience projections, and DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) inventory estimation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Streaming Meter; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: population_universe
attributes.description: Nielsen-estimated total population (persons 2+) residing within the DMA boundary. Used as the denominator for person-based ratings metrics including PUT (Persons Using Television) and TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations. Updated annually in the Nielsen universe estimates release.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates; Nielsen Universe Estimates; U.S. Census Bureau

attributes.name: primary_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code representing the predominant language spoken in the DMA (e.g., 'en' for English, 'es' for Spanish). Used for content localization decisions, Spanish-language network distribution, and audience demographic targeting.
attributes.references: ISO 639-1; ISO 639-2; Nielsen Hispanic TV Audience Measurement

attributes.name: principal_city
attributes.description: Name of the primary city or metropolitan area that anchors and names the DMA (e.g., 'New York', 'Los Angeles', 'Chicago'). Used in market identification, ad sales materials, and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: put_base_estimate
attributes.description: Nielsen baseline estimate of the percentage of persons (2+) in the DMA who are using television during an average primetime daypart. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.4612 = 46.12%). Used as a reference benchmark for PUT-based audience projections and TRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen PUT Methodology

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market coverage record was first created in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer. Used for audit trail, data lineage tracking, and compliance with SOX financial reporting controls that require data provenance.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market coverage record was most recently updated in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer. Used for change detection, incremental processing, and audit trail maintenance.

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Primary broadcast regulatory authority governing this market. 'FCC' for US markets; 'Ofcom' for UK markets; 'CRTC' for Canadian markets; 'ACMA' for Australian markets; 'other' for all other jurisdictions. Determines applicable must-carry, retransmission consent, content standards, and licensing requirements.
attributes.references: FCC Broadcast Licensing; Ofcom Broadcasting Code; CRTC Broadcasting Act

attributes.name: retransmission_consent_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether retransmission consent rules apply to broadcast stations in this market, allowing broadcasters to negotiate compensation from MVPDs for carriage of their signals. True if retransmission consent is applicable; False otherwise.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76; Cable Television Consumer Protection and Competition Act of 1992

attributes.name: state_province_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-2 two-letter state or province code of the primary state in which the DMA's principal city is located (e.g., 'NY', 'CA', 'IL'). Used for geographic segmentation, blackout rule enforcement, and retransmission consent jurisdiction determination.

attributes.name: sweeps_participation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this market participates in Nielsen sweeps periods (intensive ratings measurement periods in February, May, July, and November). True if the market is measured during sweeps; False if it is a non-sweeps market. Affects programming scheduling strategy and ad sales pricing.
attributes.references: Nielsen Sweeps Methodology; Nielsen Local TV Measurement

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the primary time zone of the DMA (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'America/Los_Angeles'). Critical for daypart scheduling, playout automation in Ericsson MediaFirst, EPG (Electronic Program Guide) alignment, and ad scheduling in Wide Orbit Traffic system.
attributes.references: IANA Time Zone Database; ATSC A/65 Program and System Information Protocol

attributes.name: total_counties
attributes.description: Total number of counties or county-equivalents included within the DMA boundary. Nielsen defines DMA boundaries at the county level. Used for geographic coverage analysis, must-carry compliance, and retransmission consent territory verification.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA County Assignment Files; FCC 47 CFR Part 76

attributes.name: tv_household_universe
attributes.description: Nielsen-estimated total number of television households within the DMA boundary. This is the principal quantitative measurement fact for the market and serves as the denominator for all local ratings calculations, GRP/TRP computations, and CPM-based ad pricing. Updated annually in the Nielsen universe estimates release.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates; Nielsen Universe Estimates

attributes.name: universe_effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which the current Nielsen universe estimates (TV household and population) became effective for this market. Used to track the currency of universe data and ensure ratings calculations use the correct denominator for the applicable measurement period.

attributes.name: universe_estimate_year
attributes.description: The calendar year for which the Nielsen universe estimates (TV household and population figures) are valid. Nielsen releases updated universe estimates annually, typically effective in the fall. Used to version and audit the universe figures used in ratings calculations.

products.name: engagement_event

Enables non-linear audience behavior analysis for programming and ad targeting.
