attributes.name: title_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the content asset (programme, episode, clip, or ad) against which this engagement event was recorded. Enables content-level audience behaviour analysis for programming decisions.
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy — Asset Metadata; EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry)

attributes.name: viewer_profile_id
attributes.description: Anonymized identifier for the audience member or household profile that generated this engagement event. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform unified profile. Used for audience segmentation and ad targeting without exposing personal identity.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Unified Profile; GDPR Article 4; CCPA §1798.140

attributes.name: ad_pod_position
attributes.description: Ordinal position of the advertisement within its ad pod (group of ads in a break) at the time of the engagement event. Populated only when is_ad_event is True. Used to analyse viewer drop-off rates by pod position and optimise ad pod sequencing for revenue assurance.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST); Wide Orbit — Ad Pod Management

attributes.name: app_version
attributes.description: Version string of the OTT/streaming application that captured the engagement event (e.g., 4.2.1). Used to correlate engagement behaviour with app release cycles and identify version-specific anomalies in audience interaction patterns.

attributes.name: bitrate_kbps
attributes.description: Actual bitrate in kilobits per second of the stream being delivered at the time of the engagement event. Sourced from Akamai CDN performance telemetry. Used alongside stream_quality to assess CDN delivery performance and its impact on audience engagement.
attributes.references: Akamai CDN — Performance Metrics; ISO 23009 MPEG-DASH

attributes.name: blackout_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether a geographic broadcast restriction (blackout) was enforced for this viewer at the time of the engagement event (True) or not (False). Supports FCC blackout compliance reporting and rights management audit trails.
attributes.references: FCC — Blackout Rules; Rightsline — Rights Availabilities; Ofcom — Territory Restrictions

attributes.name: buffering_duration_ms
attributes.description: Total duration of buffering experienced by the viewer immediately preceding or during this engagement event, in milliseconds. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform quality-of-experience telemetry. Used to correlate buffering events with pause and abandonment engagement actions.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Quality of Experience; Akamai CDN — SLA Reporting

attributes.name: content_duration_ms
attributes.description: Total duration of the content asset in milliseconds at the time of the engagement event. Used in conjunction with content_position_ms to compute completion percentage and engagement depth score. Sourced from Dalet Galaxy asset metadata.
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy — Asset Metadata; Adobe Experience Platform — Media Analytics

attributes.name: content_genre
attributes.description: Primary genre classification of the content asset associated with this engagement event (e.g., Drama, News, Sports, Comedy, Documentary). Sourced from Dalet Galaxy asset metadata. Used for genre-level audience behaviour analysis and programming acquisition decisions.
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy — Content Metadata; IAB Tech Lab — Content Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: content_position_ms
attributes.description: Playback position within the content asset at the moment the engagement event was triggered, expressed in milliseconds from the start of the content. Core EVENT_PAYLOAD_OR_VALUE for this event log. Enables precise engagement depth analysis, completion rate calculation, and identification of drop-off points.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Media Analytics; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: content_rating
attributes.description: Motion Picture Association (MPA) or TV Parental Guidelines content rating of the asset at the time of the engagement event. Used for COPPA compliance (children's content restrictions), audience demographic validation, and parental control enforcement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: G|PG|PG-13|R|NC-17|TV-Y|TV-Y7|TV-G|TV-PG|TV-14|TV-MA — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Motion Picture Association (MPA) — Content Ratings; TV Parental Guidelines; COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act)

attributes.name: data_privacy_consent
attributes.description: Viewer's data privacy consent status at the time of the engagement event, governing permissible use of this record for analytics, personalisation, and ad targeting. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform consent management. Mandatory for GDPR Article 6 lawful basis determination and CCPA opt-out compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 — Lawful Basis; GDPR Article 7 — Consent; CCPA §1798.120; COPPA

attributes.name: daypart
attributes.description: Broadcast daypart time segment in which the engagement event occurred, classified per industry-standard daypart definitions. Used for audience measurement reporting, ad sales daypart targeting, and programming scheduling decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: early_morning|daytime|early_fringe|prime_access|prime|late_news|late_fringe|overnight — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research — Daypart Definitions; IAB — Daypart Standards; Wide Orbit — Traffic Scheduling

attributes.name: device_os
attributes.description: Operating system of the device that generated the engagement event (e.g., iOS, Android, tvOS, Roku OS, Fire OS, Windows, macOS). Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform device context. Supports technical platform compatibility analysis and audience reach reporting.

attributes.name: drm_scheme
attributes.description: DRM (Digital Rights Management) protection scheme active on the content stream at the time of the engagement event. Used for rights compliance verification and to ensure content is consumed within licensed windows and territories. Supports Rightsline rights enforcement reporting.
attributes.references: Rightsline — Rights and Royalties Management; Motion Picture Association (MPA) — Anti-Piracy Standards; ISO/IEC 23009

attributes.name: engagement_depth_score
attributes.description: Normalised score (0.00–100.00) representing the depth of audience engagement at the time of the event, calculated by Adobe Experience Platform based on playback position relative to content duration, interaction frequency, and event type weighting. Key metric for non-linear audience behaviour analysis and ad targeting propensity modelling.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Engagement Scoring; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Processing lifecycle status of the engagement event record in the Silver Layer. 'valid' indicates the event passed all quality checks; 'invalid' indicates a data quality failure; 'duplicate' indicates a repeated event suppressed from analytics; 'quarantined' indicates the event is held pending investigation.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise UTC timestamp recording when the engagement action occurred on the viewer's device. Principal EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this event log entity. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used for time-series audience behaviour analysis, daypart analytics, and sweeps period reporting.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Experience Event Schema; ISO 8601

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Categorical discriminator identifying the specific audience interaction captured: play (content start/resume), pause (playback halted), seek (position jump forward), rewind (position jump backward), share (social distribution action), like (positive sentiment signal), comment (text interaction), complete (full content consumption). Core EVENT_TYPE_OR_CHANNEL field for non-linear audience behaviour analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: play|pause|seek|rewind|share|like|comment|complete — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Media Analytics; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: geo_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the viewer's geographic location at the time of the engagement event, derived from IP geolocation. Used for territorial rights compliance (blackout enforcement, holdback windows), audience reach reporting by geography, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; FCC — Geographic Broadcast Restrictions; Ofcom — Territory Licensing; GDPR Article 3

attributes.name: geo_region_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (state, province, or region) of the viewer's location at the time of the engagement event. Used for sub-national blackout enforcement, regional audience measurement, and daypart-adjusted analytics.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-2; FCC — Blackout Rules; Nielsen Media Research — Regional Audience Measurement

attributes.name: is_ad_event
attributes.description: Indicates whether this engagement event occurred during an advertisement (True) or during editorial content (False). Critical for separating content engagement metrics from ad engagement metrics in AVOD and DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) analytics.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST); Wide Orbit — Ad Scheduling

attributes.name: is_concurrent_stream
attributes.description: Indicates whether this engagement event occurred on a stream that was running concurrently with another active stream on the same viewer account (True) or not (False). Used for concurrent stream limit enforcement per subscription terms and HUT (Homes Using Television) measurement.
attributes.references: Zuora — Subscription Entitlements; Nielsen Media Research — HUT Measurement

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Indicates whether the engagement event occurred during a Nielsen sweeps measurement period (True) or outside of it (False). Sweeps periods are intensive ratings measurement windows critical for ad sales pricing and programming strategy. Enables sweeps vs. non-sweeps audience behaviour comparison.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research — Sweeps Period Calendar; FCC — Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: isan_code
attributes.description: ISAN (International Standard Audiovisual Number) of the content asset associated with this engagement event. Provides a globally unique, persistent identifier for the audiovisual work independent of platform or distribution channel. Supports rights management, royalty calculation, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 15706 — ISAN; Rightsline — Rights Management; EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry)

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: UTC timestamp when the engagement event was received and ingested by Adobe Experience Platform. Distinct from event_timestamp (client-side occurrence time). Used to measure event latency, detect clock skew, and support data quality auditing in the Silver Layer pipeline.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Data Ingestion; ISO 8601

attributes.name: referral_source
attributes.description: Channel or mechanism through which the viewer arrived at the content that triggered this engagement event. Used for audience acquisition attribution, marketing campaign effectiveness analysis, and content discovery optimisation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: direct|search|social|email|push_notification|in_app|external_link — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Journey Analytics; IAB — Attribution Standards

attributes.name: seek_from_position_ms
attributes.description: Playback position in milliseconds from which the viewer initiated a seek or rewind action. Populated only when event_type is 'seek' or 'rewind'. Combined with content_position_ms (seek-to position) to measure skip behaviour and identify content segments that audiences skip or revisit.

attributes.name: source_system_event_code
attributes.description: Original event identifier assigned by Adobe Experience Platform at the point of capture, before Silver Layer surrogate key assignment. Used for data lineage tracing, deduplication, and reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the Adobe Experience Platform source system.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Experience Event Schema; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: stream_quality
attributes.description: Adaptive bitrate (ABR) quality tier of the stream at the time of the engagement event, reflecting the HLS or MPEG-DASH rendition being delivered by the CDN. Used to correlate stream quality with engagement behaviour and identify quality-driven churn signals.
attributes.references: Akamai CDN — ABR Streaming; ATSC A/72; DVB — Adaptive Bitrate Standards; ISO 23009 MPEG-DASH

attributes.name: subscription_tier
attributes.description: Subscription or access tier of the viewer at the time of the engagement event, reflecting the monetisation model under which content was consumed. Sourced from Zuora subscription billing. Used to segment engagement behaviour by revenue tier for ARPU analysis and churn prediction.
attributes.references: Zuora — Subscription Plans; IAB — SVOD/AVOD/TVOD Definitions

products.name: guarantee
products.description: Master record of the audience delivery guarantee committed to an advertiser for a specific campaign or upfront deal — specifying the guaranteed GRP/TRP level, target demographic, measurement period, tolerance threshold, and makegood trigger conditions. Links to ad sales contracts and is reconciled against actual GRP delivery records. Central to revenue assurance and advertiser relationship management.

attributes.name: guarantee_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the audience delivery guarantee record. Primary key for the audience_guarantee data product in the Silver Layer lakehouse.

attributes.name: advertiser_id
attributes.description: Reference to the advertiser (party) to whom the audience delivery guarantee is committed. Sourced from Salesforce Media Cloud account records.
attributes.references: Salesforce Media Cloud CRM; IAB Digital Advertising Standards

attributes.name: broadcast_license_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.broadcast_license. Business justification: Audience guarantees for broadcast advertising must reference the station license for regulatory compliance (political advertising lowest unit charge, equal opportunities, public file disclosure). Guar

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the advertising campaign for which this audience delivery guarantee is established. Links to the campaign record in Salesforce Media Cloud or Wide Orbit.
attributes.references: Salesforce Media Cloud; IAB Digital Advertising Standards

attributes.name: chart_of_accounts_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.chart_of_accounts. Business justification: Audience guarantees create financial liabilities tracked in specific GL accounts for accrual accounting. Finance requires direct GL account reference for makegood reserve calculations and financial st

attributes.name: compliance_content_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.content_rating. Business justification: Guarantee fulfillment must account for content rating restrictions affecting deliverable inventory. Advertisers specify rating-appropriate placements; guarantees calculate delivery against compliant i

attributes.name: contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to talent.talent_contract. Business justification: Upfront sales negotiations frequently tie audience guarantees to specific talent participation (e.g., guaranteed GRPs for episodes featuring marquee talent). Sales teams negotiate rate premiums and de

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Makegoods incur costs (production, airtime, inventory) that must be allocated to sales operations cost centers. Finance tracks guarantee fulfillment costs separately from original campaign costs for v

attributes.name: delivery_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.delivery_channel. Business justification: Audience guarantees specify the delivery channel for audience commitment tracking and makegood calculation. Distribution and ad sales operations require channel-level guarantee attribution to reconcil

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.demographic_segment. Business justification: Guarantees target specific standardized demographic segments (e.g., A18-49, W25-54). The target_demographic_code and target_demographic_description are redundant with demographic_segment reference dat

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Each guarantee creates GL entries for revenue recognition and makegood liability accrual. Finance links guarantees to GL for audit trail, SOX compliance, and reconciliation of sold vs delivered audien

attributes.name: guarantee_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to scheduling.channel. Business justification: Audience guarantees are often negotiated at the network/channel level for upfront deals. Direct channel link enables automated guarantee reconciliation, makegood issuance by channel, and channel-speci

attributes.name: guarantee_network_channel_id
attributes.description: Reference to the television network or channel on which the guaranteed audience delivery is to be achieved. Links to the network/channel master record used in scheduling and playout systems.
attributes.references: Ericsson MediaFirst Playout; Nielsen Media Research Platform

attributes.name: ott_platform_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.ott_platform. Business justification: Audience guarantees are negotiated per OTT platform as streaming becomes a primary ad delivery vehicle. The platform_type plain-text column denormalizes ott_platform. Ad sales teams sell guaranteed GR

attributes.name: panel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.panel. Business justification: An audience delivery guarantee is measured and reconciled against a specific Nielsen panel. The guaranteed_grp, guaranteed_trp, and actual_grp_delivered values are all panel-specific metrics — their v

attributes.name: partner_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to partner.partner_partner. Business justification: Audience guarantees are contractual commitments made to specific partners (advertisers, agencies, networks). Tracking the partner receiving the guarantee is essential for makegood fulfillment and cont

attributes.name: production_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.project. Business justification: Upfront audience guarantees specify which production projects/series will deliver promised ratings. Required for makegood reconciliation, advertiser delivery reports, and sales contract fulfillment. C

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Guarantees are sold by profit centers and impact their P&L through revenue recognition and makegood costs. Finance tracks guarantee performance by profit center for business unit profitability reporti

attributes.name: program_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to scheduling.program_schedule. Business justification: Audience guarantees are tied to specific program schedules — the schedule defines the inventory against which GRP delivery is measured and reconciled. Guarantee reconciliation and makegood workflows r

attributes.name: proposal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sales.sales_proposal. Business justification: Audience guarantees are negotiated and documented in sales proposals before being formalized in orders. Proposals specify guarantee terms (GRP/TRP thresholds, makegood provisions) that become contract

attributes.name: reach_frequency_report_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.reach_frequency_report. Business justification: A guarantee is reconciled against a reach_frequency_report that validates whether the committed audience delivery was achieved. The reach_frequency_report contains the actual reach_pct, average_freque

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Guarantees must track compliance with advertising standards, political advertising disclosure rules, and FCC makegood requirements. Guarantee has political_ad_record_id and makegood_trigger_condition

attributes.name: revenue_stream_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.revenue_stream. Business justification: Audience guarantees define revenue recognition terms and makegood liability accounting. ASC 606 compliance requires linking performance obligations (guarantees) to revenue streams for proper recogniti

attributes.name: salesforce_opportunity_id
attributes.description: The opportunity identifier in Salesforce Media Cloud CRM linked to this audience guarantee. Enables traceability from the sales pipeline through to audience delivery commitment and reconciliation.

attributes.name: scheduling_daypart_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to scheduling.daypart. Business justification: Upfront guarantees specify daypart-level GRP/TRP commitments (e.g., Prime 18-49 rating guarantee). Direct daypart link enables automated delivery tracking, makegood triggering, and daypart-specific re

attributes.name: title_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to content.title. Business justification: Audience guarantees (GRP/TRP commitments to advertisers) are made against specific programs/titles. Advertisers buy guarantees tied to named shows; post-campaign reconciliation and makegood issuance r

attributes.name: actual_grp_delivered
attributes.description: The actual total GRP delivered against this guarantee as measured by the designated audience measurement source (e.g., Nielsen). Populated during and after the measurement period through reconciliation with actual delivery records. Used to determine whether the guarantee was met and whether makegoods are required.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: actual_trp_delivered
attributes.description: The actual total TRP delivered against this guarantee within the target demographic, as measured by the designated audience measurement source. Populated during reconciliation. Used alongside actual_grp_delivered to assess guarantee fulfillment for demographic-specific commitments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this audience guarantee was formally approved and activated, transitioning from draft to active status. Represents the binding commitment date for revenue recognition and contractual obligation purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; SAP S/4HANA Financial Reporting; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: cprp
attributes.description: The negotiated cost per rating point (CPRP) for this audience guarantee, expressed in the contract currency. CPRP is the standard pricing metric in broadcast advertising used to calculate the total value of the guarantee and to assess makegood compensation amounts.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this audience guarantee record was first created in the system. Audit trail field used for data lineage, compliance reporting, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the financial values associated with this audience guarantee (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Used in CPRP and total guarantee value calculations.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA Financial Standards

attributes.name: deal_type
attributes.description: Classification of the advertising deal under which this guarantee was established. Upfront refers to advance advertising sales events; scatter refers to last-minute ad inventory sales; direct, programmatic, and sponsorship represent other deal structures common in media broadcasting.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: delivery_shortfall_grp
attributes.description: The calculated difference between the guaranteed GRP level and the actual GRP delivered (guaranteed_grp minus actual_grp_delivered). A positive value indicates under-delivery and potential makegood obligation. Populated during reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the audience delivery guarantee measurement period ends. Nullable for open-ended or rolling guarantees. Defines the close of the window during which GRP/TRP delivery is tracked.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the audience delivery guarantee measurement period begins. Defines the start of the window during which GRP/TRP delivery is tracked against the committed level.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: guarantee_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the audience guarantee, used in advertiser-facing documents, contracts, and reconciliation reports. Typically referenced in Wide Orbit sales orders and Salesforce Media Cloud opportunities.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: guarantee_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the audience guarantee. Draft indicates the guarantee is being negotiated; active indicates it is in-flight; at_risk indicates delivery is trending below threshold; breached indicates the guarantee was not met and makegoods are triggered; fulfilled indicates full delivery was achieved; cancelled indicates the guarantee was voided.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: guaranteed_frequency
attributes.description: The minimum average number of times a member of the target audience is exposed to the campaign (frequency) committed to the advertiser. Frequency is the average exposures per viewer. Used alongside reach guarantees for campaigns with specific exposure objectives.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: guaranteed_grp
attributes.description: The total Gross Rating Point (GRP) level committed to the advertiser for delivery over the measurement period. GRP is the sum of ratings for all ad spots in the campaign, representing total audience exposure as a percentage of the target universe. This is the contractually obligated delivery level.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; GRP Industry Standard

attributes.name: guaranteed_reach
attributes.description: The minimum number of unique audience members (reach) committed to the advertiser over the measurement period. Reach is the count of distinct individuals exposed to the campaign at least once. Complements GRP/TRP guarantees for campaigns focused on unique audience coverage.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: guaranteed_trp
attributes.description: The total Target Rating Point (TRP) level committed to the advertiser, measured specifically against the defined target demographic segment. TRP is the GRP filtered to the target audience. Used when the guarantee is demographic-specific rather than total audience.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; TRP Industry Standard

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Indicates whether the guarantee measurement period falls within a Nielsen sweeps period (intensive ratings measurement period). Sweeps periods (February, May, July, November) carry higher audience measurement scrutiny and may affect guarantee valuation and pricing.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Sweeps Measurement Standards

attributes.name: makegood_deadline_date
attributes.description: The contractual deadline by which makegood spots must be aired to compensate for any audience delivery shortfall. Critical for revenue assurance and advertiser relationship management.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: makegood_grp_issued
attributes.description: The total GRP value of makegood (compensatory ad spots) issued to the advertiser to compensate for audience delivery shortfall. Tracked for revenue assurance and advertiser relationship management. Zero if no makegoods were required.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: makegood_trigger_condition
attributes.description: Textual description of the specific conditions under which makegood (compensatory ad spots) obligations are activated. Defines the contractual rules for when and how makegoods must be provided to the advertiser when guaranteed audience delivery is not met. Sourced from the advertising contract terms.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: nielsen_order_code
attributes.description: The external order or tracking identifier assigned by the Nielsen Media Research Platform for the audience measurement order associated with this guarantee. Used to cross-reference Nielsen ratings data and reconciliation reports.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Media Research Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional business context, special conditions, or operational notes related to this audience guarantee. May include negotiation history, special advertiser requirements, or reconciliation commentary.

attributes.name: rating_metric_type
attributes.description: Specifies the primary audience measurement metric on which this guarantee is based. GRP (Gross Rating Point) measures total audience exposure; TRP (Target Rating Point) measures exposure within the target demographic; HUT (Homes Using Television) and PUT (Persons Using Television) measure set usage; reach measures unique audience count; frequency measures average exposures per viewer.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: reconciliation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the reconciliation process comparing guaranteed audience delivery against actual GRP/TRP delivery records. Pending indicates reconciliation has not started; in_progress indicates active comparison; reconciled indicates agreement reached; disputed indicates advertiser has contested the delivery figures; closed indicates the reconciliation cycle is complete.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: tolerance_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The acceptable percentage shortfall below the guaranteed GRP/TRP level before a makegood obligation is triggered. For example, a value of 5.00 means delivery must be within 5% of the guaranteed level. Defined in the advertising contract and used in reconciliation against actual delivery records.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: total_guarantee_value
attributes.description: The total contracted monetary value of this audience guarantee, calculated as guaranteed GRP/TRP multiplied by CPRP. Represents the revenue at risk if the guarantee is not met and is central to revenue assurance and financial reconciliation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Financial Reporting; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this audience guarantee record was last modified. Used for change tracking, incremental data processing in the lakehouse Silver Layer, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: wide_orbit_order_code
attributes.description: The sales order identifier in the Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing system associated with this audience guarantee. Used for cross-system reconciliation between audience delivery records and ad scheduling/invoicing.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing System

products.name: audience_profile
products.description: Anonymized/pseudonymized master record representing a unique audience member or household identity constructed from first-party data (subscriber records, app registrations, set-top box data) and third-party enrichment (Nielsen, Adobe AEP, data clean rooms). Captures hashed identity, device graph linkage, inferred demographic attributes, content affinity scores, platform preferences, viewing recency/frequency, and consent/privacy flags per GDPR, CCPA, and COPPA. Distinct from the subscriber SSOT in the subscriber domain — this is the audience intelligence and behavioral record, not the billing or subscription identity.
products.reference: Adobe Experience Platform Profile / Audience Identity

attributes.name: audience_profile_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the audience profile record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.demographic_segment. Business justification: An audience_profile represents an anonymized audience member with inferred demographic attributes (inferred_age_band, inferred_gender, income_band). Adding demographic_segment_id links the profile to

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.market_coverage. Business justification: Audience profiles are associated with specific DMAs for geographic targeting and measurement. The dma_code should be replaced with FK to market_coverage for consistency with other products. Country_co

attributes.name: nielsen_panel_id
attributes.description: Pseudonymized identifier assigned by Nielsen Media Research to link this audience profile to a Nielsen panel household or individual. Enables direct integration of Nielsen ratings, GRP/TRP, and demographic data. Null for non-panel profiles.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: ad_receptivity_score
attributes.description: Propensity score (0.00–100.00) indicating this audience member's likelihood to engage with advertising content, derived from behavioral signals in Adobe AEP and viewing pattern analysis. Used by ad sales teams for premium audience packaging and CPM pricing optimization.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Propensity Scoring; IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Salesforce Media Cloud

attributes.name: aep_profile_code
attributes.description: Unique profile identifier from Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) used to link behavioral engagement data, segment memberships, and journey analytics to this audience profile. Enables personalization and digital engagement enrichment.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Real-Time Customer Profile; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: avg_session_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Average duration in minutes of a single viewing session for this audience member, derived from set-top box or streaming platform telemetry. Represents Time Spent Viewing (TSV) at the individual level. Used for engagement scoring and content performance analytics.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Time Spent Viewing (TSV); Adobe Experience Platform Analytics

attributes.name: ccpa_opt_out
attributes.business_glossary_term: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Opt-Out Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this California-resident audience member has exercised their CCPA right to opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information. When TRUE, this profile must be excluded from data sharing with third-party ad networks and data clean rooms.
attributes.references: CCPA Section 1798.120 (Right to Opt-Out); California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA)

attributes.name: consent_last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent change to any consent or privacy flag (GDPR consent status, CCPA opt-out, COPPA flag) for this audience profile. Critical for regulatory audit trails demonstrating timely consent management and data processing compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent); CCPA Section 1798.120; COPPA 16 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: content_affinity_genre
attributes.description: Top inferred content genre affinity for this audience member (e.g., 'news', 'sports', 'drama', 'reality', 'documentary'), derived from viewing history and behavioral signals in Adobe AEP. Used for content recommendation, programming decisions, and audience-targeted ad sales. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: news|sports|drama|comedy|reality|documentary|entertainment|kids|lifestyle|sci_fi — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Segment Builder; Nielsen Content Ratings; IAB Content Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: coppa_protected
attributes.business_glossary_term: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) Protected Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this audience profile is subject to COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) protections, meaning the inferred or declared age is under 13. When TRUE, ad targeting, data sharing, and behavioral tracking are strictly restricted per COPPA compliance requirements.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) — 15 U.S.C. §§ 6501–6506; FCC Children's Television Rules

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the audience member's country of residence. Used for rights windowing, content holdback enforcement, GDPR/CCPA jurisdictional compliance, and international distribution analytics.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; GDPR Article 3 (Territorial Scope); CCPA

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this audience profile record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse, either through initial identity resolution, panel enrollment, or first-party data ingestion. Audit trail for data lineage and GDPR data minimization compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Minimization); Internal Data Governance Audit Standard

attributes.name: data_clean_room_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this audience profile is eligible for inclusion in data clean room matching operations with advertising partners. Eligibility is determined by consent status, CCPA opt-out flag, COPPA protection status, and contractual data sharing agreements.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Data Clean Rooms Standards; GDPR Article 26 (Joint Controllers); CCPA

attributes.name: daypart_preference
attributes.description: Preferred daypart (time segment of the broadcast day) during which this audience member most frequently views content. Dayparts are standard broadcast industry time segments used for ad scheduling, upfront sales, and audience guarantee reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Daypart Definitions; Wide Orbit Traffic System; IAB Video Ad Standards

attributes.name: device_graph_code
attributes.description: Cross-device graph linkage identifier that associates this audience profile with a cluster of known devices (smart TV, mobile, desktop, STB). Sourced from identity resolution providers or Adobe AEP device graph. Enables multi-screen reach and frequency measurement.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Addressability & Identity; Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service

attributes.name: enrichment_source_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the third-party enrichment data package (e.g., Nielsen demographic file version, Adobe AEP segment refresh batch ID) used to populate inferred attributes on this profile. Enables data lineage tracing and reproducibility of audience segment definitions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Data Delivery Versioning; Adobe Experience Platform Data Governance

attributes.name: gdpr_consent_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Consent Status
attributes.description: Current GDPR consent status for processing this audience member's personal data for audience measurement and advertising purposes. 'granted' permits processing; 'denied' or 'withdrawn' restricts processing; 'not_applicable' for non-EU audience members. Drives data processing eligibility.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis); GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent); European Audiovisual Observatory

attributes.name: household_size
attributes.description: Estimated number of persons in the audience household, derived from Nielsen panel data or set-top box signals. Used in HUT (Homes Using Television) and PUT (Persons Using Television) calculations for audience measurement reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — HUT/PUT Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement

attributes.name: hut_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this household-level audience profile is eligible to be counted in HUT (Homes Using Television) calculations. HUT measures the percentage of TV-equipped homes actively watching television during a given time period, a foundational metric for broadcast ratings.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — HUT Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: identity_confidence_score
attributes.description: Confidence score (0.00–100.00) representing the reliability of the identity resolution that constructed this audience profile. Higher scores indicate stronger deterministic matching (e.g., authenticated login); lower scores indicate probabilistic device-graph inference. Used to qualify profiles for premium ad targeting.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Addressability & Identity Framework; Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service

attributes.name: identity_hash
attributes.description: SHA-256 pseudonymized hash of the audience member's primary identity (e.g., email or subscriber ID) used for cross-platform identity resolution without exposing raw PII. Enables privacy-safe linkage across Nielsen, Adobe AEP, and first-party data sources.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4 & Article 25 (Privacy by Design); CCPA Section 1798.140

attributes.name: identity_source
attributes.description: Originating source of the audience identity construction: 'first_party' (subscriber or app registration data), 'nielsen' (Nielsen Media Research panel linkage), 'adobe_aep' (Adobe Experience Platform profile), 'set_top_box' (STB device-level data), 'clean_room' (data clean room match), or 'modeled' (probabilistic inference).
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Adobe Experience Platform; IAB Data Transparency Standards

attributes.name: income_band
attributes.description: Inferred household income band derived from third-party demographic enrichment (Nielsen, data clean rooms). Used for premium audience segmentation in upfront and scatter market ad sales, enabling CPM pricing differentiation by audience affluence.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Enrichment; IAB Audience Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: inferred_age_band
attributes.description: Inferred age demographic band for the audience member, derived from Nielsen panel data, set-top box signals, or modeled enrichment. Used for GRP/TRP demographic targeting and ad sales audience guarantees. Not directly collected from the individual.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Segmentation; IAB Audience Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: inferred_gender
attributes.description: Inferred gender of the audience member derived from panel data or modeled signals. Used for demographic audience targeting in ad sales (GRP/TRP calculations) and programming decisions. Not directly collected.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Segmentation; IAB Audience Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: last_seen_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent observed audience activity event (viewing session, app interaction, or platform login) for this profile. Used to determine audience recency, drive re-engagement campaigns, and calculate viewing recency metrics.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Profile Last Activity; Nielsen Audience Engagement

attributes.name: nielsen_grp_index
attributes.description: Indexed GRP (Gross Rating Point) score for this audience profile relative to the total population, sourced from Nielsen Media Research. A GRP index above 100 indicates above-average exposure to rated content. Used in ad sales audience guarantees and upfront negotiations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — GRP Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: panel_weight_factor
attributes.description: Statistical weighting factor assigned by Nielsen to this panel member profile to project panel observations to the total population. Applied in GRP, TRP, HUT, and PUT calculations. Null for non-panel (modeled or first-party only) profiles.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Weighting Methodology; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: platform_preference
attributes.description: Primary viewing platform preference inferred from behavioral signals: 'linear_tv' (traditional scheduled broadcast), 'svod' (Subscription Video On Demand), 'avod' (Advertising-Supported VOD), 'tvod' (Transactional VOD), 'fast' (Free Ad-Supported Streaming TV), 'ott' (Over-The-Top), 'mvpd' (Multichannel Video Programming Distributor), or 'vmvpd' (Virtual MVPD). Drives distribution strategy and ad product targeting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_tv|svod|avod|tvod|fast|ott|mvpd|vmvpd — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Spend Report; ATSC 3.0 Standards; DVB Project

attributes.name: primary_device_type
attributes.description: The primary device type through which this audience member most frequently consumes content, derived from device graph and behavioral data. Used for CDN delivery optimization, ad format targeting, and platform analytics.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Device Type Taxonomy; Akamai CDN Analytics

attributes.name: profile_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the audience profile. 'suppressed' indicates a privacy opt-out or regulatory hold; 'pending_consent' indicates consent collection is in progress; 'purged' indicates the record has been anonymized per GDPR/CCPA erasure request.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure); CCPA Section 1798.105; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: profile_type
attributes.description: Classification of the audience profile record: 'individual' (single person identity), 'household' (aggregated household unit), 'panel_member' (Nielsen or equivalent panel participant), or 'modeled' (synthetically constructed from behavioral signals without direct identity linkage).
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Audience Segmentation Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: sweeps_period_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this audience profile's measurement data was captured during a Nielsen Sweeps period (intensive ratings measurement period: February, May, July, November). Sweeps data carries higher statistical weight in ratings calculations and programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sweeps Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: trp_index
attributes.description: Indexed TRP (Target Rating Point) score representing this audience member's contribution to a specific demographic target group's rating. Distinct from GRP in that it measures reach within a defined target demographic. Used for demographic-specific ad campaign planning and post-campaign analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — TRP Methodology; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this audience profile record, triggered by enrichment refresh, consent status change, identity graph update, or behavioral signal ingestion. Used for data freshness monitoring and incremental processing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Accuracy); Internal Data Governance Audit Standard; Adobe Experience Platform

attributes.name: viewing_recency_days
attributes.description: Number of days since this audience member last engaged with any content on any tracked platform. Used for audience recency segmentation, churn prediction, and re-engagement campaign targeting. Lower values indicate more recently active audiences.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Recency-Frequency-Monetary (RFM) Segmentation; Nielsen Audience Engagement Metrics

attributes.name: weekly_viewing_frequency
attributes.description: Average number of distinct viewing sessions per week for this audience member, calculated over a rolling 4-week window. Represents the Frequency dimension of audience measurement (average exposures per viewer). Used in reach and frequency reporting for ad campaign delivery.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Reach and Frequency Methodology; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

products.name: segment
products.description: Master record for a defined, reusable audience segment built from demographic, behavioral, and psychographic criteria for use in ad targeting, programming strategy, and content personalization. Captures segment name, definition logic, estimated size, demographic composition, platform applicability, activation status, and data source (Nielsen, Adobe AEP, first-party). Distinct from demographic_segment (which is a reference classification) — this is an operationally managed, business-owned targeting segment.
products.reference: Adobe AEP Segment / Nielsen Audience Segment

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the audience segment record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this master resource entity.

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.demographic_segment. Business justification: A segment (activation/targeting segment) is built from demographic, behavioral, and psychographic criteria. Adding demographic_segment_id links the activation segment to its Nielsen demographic_segmen

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Segment activation_status and dai_eligible flags require compliance

attributes.name: activation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the segment governing whether it is available for use in ad targeting, campaign activation, or content personalization. 'draft' indicates under construction; 'pending_review' awaits compliance or data governance approval; 'active' is live and deployable; 'inactive' is suspended; 'archived' is retired.

attributes.name: aep_segment_code

attributes.name: age_range_max
attributes.description: Maximum age (inclusive) of the primary demographic target for this segment, expressed in years. Used with age_range_min to define the Nielsen demographic cell. A null value indicates an open-ended upper bound (e.g., '55+' segments).

attributes.name: age_range_min

attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Demographic Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the data governance or compliance approver who authorized this segment for activation, particularly for segments involving sensitive demographic data, COPPA-restricted audiences, or GDPR-regulated EU audiences. Supports audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Accountability Principle); COPPA Compliance; Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this segment received formal data governance or compliance approval for activation. Distinct from created_timestamp — captures the approval lifecycle event. Required for GDPR accountability documentation and internal audit trails. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Accountability Principle); Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: content_genre_affinity

Sourced from Nielsen viewing behavior data or Adobe AEP content interaction signals. Informs content acquisition decisions and ad pod placement strategy.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Content Affinity Reports; IAB Content Taxonomy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this audience segment record was first created in the system. Serves as the audit creation timestamp for data lineage, governance, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Confidentiality); SOX Section 404 (Internal Controls); Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the primary data origin used to construct the segment. 'nielsen' indicates Nielsen Media Research Platform ratings and demographic data; 'adobe_aep' indicates Adobe Experience Platform behavioral profiles; 'first_party' indicates proprietary subscriber or registration data; 'third_party' indicates licensed external data; 'hybrid' indicates a combination of multiple sources.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Adobe Experience Platform; IAB Data Transparency Standards

attributes.name: daypart_applicability
attributes.description: Broadcast daypart(s) for which this segment is most relevant or has been validated, expressed as a comma-delimited list of standard daypart labels (e.g., 'primetime,late_night'). attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Definitions; Wide Orbit Traffic System Daypart Standards

attributes.name: definition_logic
attributes.description: The rule-based or SQL/JSON expression that defines segment membership criteria as implemented in Adobe AEP or Nielsen. attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Segment Builder; Nielsen Audience Workbench

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: The date from which this segment definition is considered valid and available for business use. Segments may be pre-built ahead of upfront sales seasons or campaign launches. Enables temporal validity management for segment versioning and historical reporting.

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: The date after which this segment definition is no longer valid for new activations. Null indicates an open-ended segment with no planned expiry. Used to manage seasonal segments (e.g., sweeps-period segments), campaign-specific segments, and segments tied to expiring data licensing agreements.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Internal Data Governance Standards; IAB Audience Data Lifecycle

attributes.name: estimated_reach
attributes.description: Estimated number of unique individuals (persons or households) who qualify for this segment at the time of last refresh. Reach is a core Nielsen and IAB metric used in ad sales proposals, GRP/TRP calculations, and CPM pricing. Distinct from impressions — counts unique audience members, not exposures.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Audience Measurement Standards; IAB Reach and Frequency Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: estimated_reach_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the estimated_reach figure. 'persons' aligns with Nielsen PUT (Persons Using Television) methodology; 'households' aligns with HUT (Homes Using Television); 'devices' applies to digital/OTT platform segments measured by device-level identity.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research HUT/PUT Measurement Standards; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: gender_target
attributes.description: Gender composition target for the segment as defined in Nielsen demographic cells and ad sales targeting parameters. 'all' indicates gender-neutral targeting. Used in GRP (Gross Rating Point) and TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations for ad campaign planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Demographic Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: grp_index
attributes.description: The GRP (Gross Rating Point) index value representing this segment's relative audience weight as a percentage of the total universe. GRP is a fundamental media planning metric equal to Reach × Frequency. Used in upfront and scatter market ad sales to price inventory and measure campaign delivery against this segment.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research GRP Methodology; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: hut_put_basis
attributes.description: Indicates whether the segment's reach and rating metrics are calculated on a HUT (Homes Using Television) or PUT (Persons Using Television) basis. HUT is household-level measurement; PUT is person-level. This distinction governs how GRP/TRP values are interpreted and how the segment is applied in Nielsen-based ad sales planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research HUT/PUT Methodology Standards

attributes.name: income_bracket
attributes.description: Household income tier associated with the segment's demographic composition, used in premium ad targeting and CPM (Cost Per Mille) pricing. Expressed as a standardized range label (e.g., '$75K-$100K HHI', '$100K+ HHI'). Sourced from Nielsen MRI-Simmons or first-party subscriber data. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: under_25k|25k_50k|50k_75k|75k_100k|100k_150k|150k_plus — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: is_dai_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment is approved and technically configured for use in DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) workflows on OTT and streaming platforms. DAI-eligible segments can be activated in real-time ad decisioning systems integrated with Akamai CDN and programmatic ad servers for addressable advertising.
attributes.references: SCTE-130 Dynamic Ad Insertion Standard; IAB VAST/VMAP Standards; Akamai DAI Integration

attributes.name: is_sweeps_validated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment's reach and demographic composition estimates have been validated using Nielsen Sweeps period data (the intensive ratings measurement periods in February, May, July, and November). Sweeps-validated segments carry higher confidence for upfront ad sales commitments and programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Sweeps Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: last_refresh_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the segment membership, reach estimates, and demographic composition were last recalculated from source data. Used to assess data freshness for ad sales proposals and campaign activation. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Segment Evaluation Logs; Nielsen Audience Measurement Refresh Standards

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this audience segment record was last updated. Tracks changes to segment definition, status, reach estimates, or compliance flags. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and audit trail maintenance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); SOX Section 404; Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: nielsen_segment_code
attributes.description: The corresponding segment or audience cell identifier within the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Enables direct linkage to Nielsen ratings data, GRP/TRP delivery reports, and demographic reach/frequency outputs. Used for reconciliation between internal segment definitions and Nielsen-measured audience delivery.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform API; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional business context, caveats, or operational notes about the segment that do not fit structured fields. Examples include data quality warnings, known limitations of the definition logic, special handling instructions for ad sales, or notes on upcoming segment retirement.

attributes.name: owner_team
attributes.description: The business team or department that owns and is accountable for this segment's definition, quality, and lifecycle management (e.g., 'Ad Sales Research', 'Audience Analytics', 'Programming Strategy', 'Digital Marketing'). Used for data governance, access control, and segment portfolio management.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy; IAB Data Transparency Standards

attributes.name: platform_applicability
attributes.description: Comma-delimited list of distribution platforms for which this segment is valid and activated (e.g., 'linear,ott,avod,svod,fast'). Governs where the segment can be applied for ad targeting or content personalization across Linear, OTT (Over-The-Top), AVOD (Advertising-Supported Video On Demand), SVOD (Subscription Video On Demand), and FAST (Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television) channels. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear|ott|avod|svod|tvod|fast|social|digital_display — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST); IAB Audience Taxonomy; ATSC 3.0 Targeted Advertising Standards

attributes.name: refresh_frequency
attributes.description: How frequently the segment membership and reach estimates are recalculated and updated from source systems (Nielsen, Adobe AEP, or first-party data). Governs data freshness SLAs for ad targeting activation. 'real_time' applies to DAI-eligible programmatic segments; 'daily' is standard for digital; 'weekly/monthly' for Nielsen-based linear segments.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Segment Evaluation Modes; Nielsen Audience Refresh Standards; IAB Data Freshness Guidelines

attributes.name: segment_category
attributes.description: Business-facing category grouping segments for portfolio management and reporting (e.g., 'Ad Targeting', 'Programming Strategy', 'Content Personalization', 'Subscriber Retention', 'Regulatory Reporting'). Enables segment library organization in Salesforce Media Cloud and Adobe AEP. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ad_targeting|programming_strategy|content_personalization|subscriber_retention|regulatory_reporting|audience_research — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Audience Taxonomy; Adobe Experience Platform Segment Classification

attributes.name: segment_code
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the segment used across systems such as Adobe Experience Platform (AEP), Nielsen, and Salesforce Media Cloud. Serves as the canonical cross-system reference code (e.g., 'SEG-DEMO-F25-54-OTT').
attributes.references: IAB Audience Taxonomy; Adobe Experience Platform Segment Naming Standards

attributes.name: segment_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the segment's business purpose, defining criteria, and intended use cases. Provides context for ad sales teams, programmers, and data analysts on what the segment represents and how it should be applied.

attributes.name: segment_name

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the segment by the primary methodology used to define it. Demographic segments are built on age/gender/HUT criteria; behavioral on viewing patterns; psychographic on interests/attitudes; contextual on content affinity; lookalike on modeled similarity to a seed audience.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Taxonomy; Nielsen Audience Segmentation Standards

attributes.name: trp_index
attributes.description: The TRP (Target Rating Point) index value representing this segment's rating within its specific target demographic universe. TRP is the targeted equivalent of GRP, measuring delivery efficiency against the defined demographic cell. Critical for ad sales pricing, makegoods calculations, and CPRP (Cost Per Rating Point) negotiations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research TRP Methodology; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Monotonically incrementing version counter for the segment definition. Incremented each time the segment's definition logic, demographic criteria, or platform applicability is materially changed. Enables segment versioning for historical campaign attribution — ad campaigns reference the segment version active at time of booking.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy; Adobe Experience Platform Segment Versioning

products.name: segment_membership
products.description: This association product represents the membership relationship between audience_profile and segment. It captures the operational assignment of individual audience profiles to targeting segments for ad delivery, content personalization, and campaign activation. Each record links one audience profile to one segment with membership lifecycle attributes, activation status, and scoring metadata that exist only in the context of this specific profile-segment assignment.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting operations, audience segment membership is a core operational concept actively managed by audience intelligence and ad operations teams. A single audience profile simultaneously belongs to multiple segments (e.g., 'Sports Enthusiasts', 'High Income HH', 'Prime Time Viewers'), and each segment contains thousands to millions of audience profiles. The business explicitly tracks membership lifecycle (when profiles enter/exit segments), membership scores (how strongly they match criteria), and activation status (whether the membership is available for ad targeting). This is evidenced by the aep_segment_membership attribute on audience_profile, which is a denormalized representation of this M:N relationship.

Station

attributes.name: close_date

attributes.name: closed_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the opportunity was marked as closed-won or closed-lost. Null for open opportunities. Used for sales cycle analysis and win rate calculation.

attributes.name: competitive_displacement
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing competitive intelligence about which competitor this deal may displace or compete against. Used for win/loss analysis and competitive strategy.

attributes.name: cpm_rate
attributes.description: Cost per thousand impressions rate negotiated for this opportunity. Standard pricing metric for digital and streaming advertising. Expressed in currency per 1,000 impressions.

attributes.name: cprp_rate
attributes.description: Cost per rating point negotiated for linear TV or radio buys. Standard pricing metric for broadcast advertising. Calculated as total cost divided by total GRPs delivered.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this opportunity record was first created in Salesforce Media Cloud. Used for lead-to-close cycle time analysis and pipeline velocity tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the estimated value (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Supports multi-currency deal tracking for international sales.

attributes.name: daypart
attributes.description: Time segment of the broadcast day targeted by this opportunity. Daypart classification affects pricing and audience demographics. attributes.name: deal_type

attributes.name: demographic_target
attributes.description: Primary demographic audience segment targeted by this campaign (e.g., 'Adults 18-49', 'Women 25-54', 'Men 18-34'). Used for audience guarantee and measurement alignment.

attributes.name: estimated_value
attributes.description: Total estimated revenue value of the opportunity in USD. For advertising deals, represents total campaign spend; for content licensing, represents license fee. Used for revenue forecasting and quota tracking.

attributes.name: flight_end_date
attributes.description: Planned end date for the advertising campaign or content distribution window. Defines the duration of the media buy or license period.

attributes.name: flight_start_date
attributes.description: Planned start date for the advertising campaign or content distribution window. For advertising, marks the beginning of the ad flight; for content licensing, marks the start of the license window.

attributes.name: forecast_category
attributes.description: Sales forecast category indicating confidence level for revenue recognition. Pipeline = early stage; Best Case = likely but not committed; Commit = high confidence; Closed = won. Used for revenue forecasting rollups.

attributes.name: is_upfront
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this opportunity is part of the annual upfront sales season. True = upfront commitment; False = scatter market or other deal type. Used for upfront tracking and reporting.

attributes.name: last_activity_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent sales activity (call, email, meeting) logged against this opportunity. Used for pipeline hygiene monitoring and stale opportunity identification.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this opportunity record. Used for data freshness validation and change tracking. Updated automatically on any field modification.

attributes.name: lead_source
attributes.description: Origin channel of this sales opportunity. Tracks how the lead was generated for marketing attribution and lead source ROI analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: inbound|outbound|referral|event|partner|renewal|upsell — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: loss_notes
attributes.description: Free-text detailed explanation of why the opportunity was lost. Captures competitive intelligence, pricing feedback, and strategic insights for future deals.

attributes.name: loss_reason
attributes.description: Primary reason for losing the opportunity if stage is closed-lost. Used for loss analysis, competitive intelligence, and sales process improvement. Null for won or open opportunities.

attributes.name: next_step
attributes.description: Description of the next action or milestone required to advance this opportunity. Used for sales activity tracking and pipeline hygiene. Updated regularly by sales executive.

attributes.name: opportunity_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the sales opportunity, typically including advertiser name, campaign type, and time period (e.g., 'Acme Corp Q4 Upfront Buy').

attributes.name: opportunity_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the opportunity, typically auto-generated in format OPP-YYYYNNNN. Used in sales communications and reporting.
attributes.references: Salesforce Media Cloud Opportunity Naming Convention

attributes.name: probability
attributes.description: Estimated likelihood of closing this opportunity as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00). Typically aligned with stage (e.g., Proposal = 40%, Negotiation = 60%). Used for weighted pipeline forecasting.

attributes.name: product_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the media product being sold. Linear TV = traditional broadcast; Digital Video = online video ads; Streaming = OTT/SVOD/AVOD inventory; Content Licensing = rights to broadcast content. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_tv|digital_video|streaming|radio|podcast|display|social|sponsorship|content_licensing — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Media Taxonomy, MPA Content Classification

attributes.name: requires_makegood
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this opportunity includes makegood provisions for audience delivery shortfalls. True = makegoods may be required if audience guarantees are not met. Used for inventory planning.

attributes.name: stage
attributes.description: Current stage in the sales pipeline lifecycle. Tracks progression from initial prospecting through closure. Used for pipeline forecasting and sales funnel analysis.
attributes.references: Salesforce Media Cloud Sales Process Framework

attributes.name: target_grp
attributes.description: Target Gross Rating Points representing the total audience reach multiplied by frequency. Standard metric for linear TV and radio campaign planning. One GRP = 1% of the target audience reached.

attributes.name: target_impressions
attributes.description: Total number of ad impressions committed in this opportunity. Primary delivery metric for digital video, streaming, and programmatic deals. Measured in thousands or millions.

products.name: avail

Updated in near-real-time as holds are placed and orders confirmed.

domains.name: billing
domains.description: Single source of truth for all revenue transactions — subscriber invoices, advertising billing, carriage fee invoicing, syndication license fees, and payment processing. Manages billing cycles, payment methods, PCI DSS-compliant card processing, revenue recognition (ASC 606), dispute management, and makegoods. Integrates with Zuora (subscription billing), Wide Orbit (ad billing), and SAP S/4HANA (financial posting).

products.name: invoice

Captures invoice number, billing period, total amount due, currency, tax amounts, invoice status (draft, issued, paid, disputed, void), due date, payment terms, revenue category (subscription, advertising, carriage, syndication), ASC 606 revenue recognition period, and source system reference (Zuora, Wide Orbit, SAP S/4HANA). Supports stream-specific extended attributes: subscription plan/proration for SVOD billing, Wide Orbit order ID/ISCI codes for ad billing, MVPD subscriber count basis for carriage fees, and license window/installment schedule for syndication. Serves as the SSOT for all billing documents across all revenue streams.

attributes.name: service_period_start_date

attributes.name: service_type

attributes.name: tax_code

attributes.name: unit_of_measure

attributes.name: unit_rate

attributes.name: profit_center_id

attributes.name: applied_amount

attributes.name: authorization_code
attributes.description: Authorization code returned by the payment processor or card issuer confirming approval of the transaction.

attributes.name: bank_transaction_reference
attributes.description: Reference number provided by the bank for wire transfers, ACH transactions, or check deposits. Used for bank reconciliation.

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The channel or interface through which the payment was submitted (web portal, mobile app, IVR, mail, in-person, API, batch import). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: web_portal|mobile_app|ivr|mail|in_person|api|batch_import — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: check_number
attributes.description: Check number for payments made by paper check. Used for reconciliation and tracking.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this payment record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the payment transaction (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR, CAD).

attributes.name: dispute_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment dispute or chargeback was initiated. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: failure_reason

attributes.name: gateway
attributes.description: Name of the payment gateway or processor used to handle the transaction (e.g., Stripe, Authorize.Net, PayPal, Adyen).

attributes.name: gateway_transaction_reference

attributes.name: gl_posting_date

attributes.name: is_autopay

attributes.name: is_disputed
